content:
customer-success: Heads-up — we have 3 customers reporting a sudden p99 spike on text/generate for redwood-large-v1 after last night's runtime rollout. p95 ~1.15x, p99 ~2.4x. They saw timeouts in some tail requests. Logs attached by one customer (anonymized).

maria: seeing the same in dashboards, noticed a correlation with the kernel selection change pushed at 02:05 UTC that enables the new attention heuristics (prefer SDPA when sequence_len > 1024). Could be the SDPA fallback thrashing for mixed seq lengths.

raj: deploy details: rollout id rollout-2026-03-15-02, change was `attn.heuristics=v2` + compile flag `FAST_MATH=true` for the kernels. We did canary on 10% then promoted. No errors in CI perf, but those tests used uniform seq lengths (1024).

sophie: useful repro request — can we get a minimal repro script or a request trace? If customers can share a sampled request we can run locally with the same model + kernel flags.

customer-success: provided a sample payload (sanitized). 2-3k tokens with many short requests interleaved. They said issue appears with bursty traffic and varying seq lengths.

bench-bot: ran a quick baseline on a dev GPU with the sample workload. With attn.heuristics=v1 (legacy FlashAttn-first): p99=220ms. With heuristics=v2 (SDPA-prefers): p99=520ms and memory churn spikes. Raw logs:

```
[perf] seq_len=256 -> kernel=flash_attn_v1 lat=45ms
[perf] seq_len=2048 -> kernel=sdpa_v2 lat=380ms
[mem] kv_cache_realloc count=12 -> 1.2GB/sec churn
```

raj: that memory churn line is worrying — SDPA kernel path does more dynamic allocations in our runtime. Might be fragmentation with mixed lengths.

maria: mitigation options I see:
- roll back attn.heuristics to v1 (instant config toggle) — fastest but loses potential perf on long-seq workloads
- force flash_attn for this customer group via routing profile (route-by-customer) — per-customer toggle
- disable FAST_MATH compile flag and recompile kernels (longer, infra busy)

ales: I can flip per-customer kernel preference quickly. Which customers to target? customer-success provided a list of three paying accounts hit hardest.

sophie: short repro steps for eng to reproduce locally (I ran these):
1) checkout runtime@rollout-2026-03-15
2) start serving with env `ATTN_HEURISTICS=v2` and `FAST_MATH=1`
3) run load generator `python tools/load_gen.py --trace samples/customer_samples.json --concurrency 40`
4) observe p99 with `curl http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep request_p99`

kevin: I propose immediate mitigation: route the three affected customers to a legacy kernel profile (flash_attn) and pause the rollout to remaining hosts. Then run a targeted repro + mem-prof to confirm.

maria: agreed. @ales please apply per-customer toggle and mark as urgent.

ales: done — toggled route preference. Commands used:
```
# admin API
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood/api/admin/feature-flags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"scope":"customer","id":"acct-REDACTED","flags":{"attn.kernel_preference":"flash_attn"}}'
```
Response: 200 OK. Rolling back canary to 10% now.

infra-bot: deploy rollback scheduled: rollout-2026-03-15 -> paused; canary scaled down from 100% -> 10% at 03:10 UTC.

bench-bot: after route toggle p99 for affected tenants dropped from ~520ms -> ~210ms within two minutes. CPU/GPU memory stabilized.

sophie: root cause hypothesis: heuristics v2 selects SDPA for >1024 but our allocator and KV cache resizing logic isn't amortizing well for mixed-length bursts, causing reallocs and page faults which explode tail latency. Also FAST_MATH changed fp behavior that allowed different codegen paths that are slower for certain kernels.

raj: next steps:
- short-term: keep canary paused and per-customer kernel preference enforced (done)
- mid-term: revert heuristics change or improve allocator (need eng-ml/runtime action)
- long-term: add microbench harness with mixed seq-length traces for CI perf gating

maria: assigning owners: raj -> roll out allocator profiling change, sophie -> write mixed-seq CI test and reproduction harness, kevin -> coordinate with customers + CS comms.

customer-success: told customers we've applied a routing fix and are investigating deeper. They asked for ETA on a full fix — we gave ~48-72h to validate allocator improvements or revert.

ales: logging/telemetry action: I added a new per-request tag `attn_kernel` to trace so we can measure p99 by kernel. Instrumented on canary hosts.

bench-bot: example metric query to monitor:
`sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{le=\"0.5\",attn_kernel=\"sdpa_v2\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_count{attn_kernel=\"sdpa_v2\"}[5m]))`

maria: thanks team. We'll keep this thread updated. If allocator fix looks risky we need to plan a full revert of heuristics v2 and a clean recompile with FAST_MATH toggled off for a proper perf comparison.

kevin: note for postmortem: include the CI blind spot (uniform seq len tests) and add explicit mixed workload tests. Also document rollback playbook and per-customer routing steps.

sophie: I'll open the follow-up tickets and link perf artifacts. Drafting repro + CI test now. :white_check_mark:

maria: closing the active incident once p99 stable for 2 hours on affected tenants. Current status: stable after routing toggle at 03:15 UTC. Will update in 60m.

customer-success: thanks, will update customers and watch for any new reports. :thumbsup:
